blocks.prompt: 2 (a) The displacement-time graph of a moving car is shown in Fig. 7.10. The car changes its direction during the journey, and its motion occurs in three distinct phases. What is the car's velocity in each phase?
blocks.explanation:
We must read the graph and find the velocity in each of the three straight phases.
Given: Figure 7.10 (one small square = 1 unit of time across and 10 km up).
Plan: read the corner points, then velocity = slope of each straight piece.
steps:
Given: the displacement-time graph of Figure 7.10.
To find: the velocity in each phase.
Method: velocity = slope of the displacement-time graph (7.1.4). Each phase is a straight line, so the velocity in it is constant.

Read the corner points
\[O(0, 0),\ A(3, 60)\]
\[B(7, 0),\ C\left(\tfrac{26}{3}, -25\right)\]
Why: the line rises to its highest point, 60 km, at \(t = 3\); it then falls through the grid point (5, 30), cuts the time axis at \(t = 7\) and ends halfway between the \(-20\) and \(-30\) lines. The three phases are O to A, A to B and B to C.

Phase 1 (O to A)
\[v_1 = \dfrac{60 - 0}{3 - 0}\]
\[= 20\text{ km/h}\]
Why: a rising line has a positive slope: the car moves away from the start.

Phase 2 (A to B)
\[v_2 = \dfrac{0 - 60}{7 - 3}\]
\[= \dfrac{-60}{4} = -15\text{ km/h}\]
Why: a falling line has a negative slope: the car has turned round and moves back towards the start.

Phase 3 (B to C)
\[v_3 = \dfrac{-25 - 0}{\frac{26}{3} - 7}\]
\[= \dfrac{-25}{5/3} = -15\text{ km/h}\]
Why: B to C lies on the same straight line as A to B, so the slope is the same. The car keeps moving backward, now past the start (\(x\) negative).

Check with the grid point (5, 30)
\[\dfrac{30 - 60}{5 - 3} = -15 \;\checkmark\]
Why: any two points of the same straight line give the same slope.
blocks.final_answer: Phase 1: \(20\) km/h; phase 2: \(-15\) km/h; phase 3: \(-15\) km/h (the minus sign means moving backward at 15 km/h)

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Figure 7.10 labels the displacement in km but the time in seconds (s). That would make the first velocity 20 km per second (72 000 km/h), which is impossible for a car. The time must be in hours, so we give the velocities in km/h. (If the printed seconds are kept, every number on this page stays the same and only km/h becomes km/s.) The figure also does not mark where the journey ends; we take the end of the drawn line, \(x = -25\) km, which the line reaches at \(t = 26/3\) h.

blocks.prompt: 2 (b) The displacement-time graph of a moving car is shown in Fig. 7.10. The car changes its direction during the journey, and its motion occurs in three distinct phases. When did the car pass its starting point again?
blocks.explanation:
The car is at its starting point when its displacement is zero again.
Given: the falling line through A(3, 60) with slope \(-15\).
Plan: write the equation of that line and put \(x = 0\).
steps:
Given: the falling line passes through \(A(3, 60)\) with slope \(-15\).
To find: the time \(t > 0\) at which \(x = 0\).
Method: at the starting point the displacement is 0, i.e. the graph meets the time axis.

Equation of the falling line
\[x - 60 = -15(t - 3)\]
\[x = 105 - 15t\]
Why: point-slope form of a straight line with the point A and the slope found in (a).

Put \(x = 0\)
\[0 = 105 - 15t\]
\[t = 7\]
Why: displacement zero means the car is back at its starting point.

Check
\[x(7) = 105 - 105 = 0 \;\checkmark\]
Why: the graph cuts the time axis at \(t = 7\) (point B).
blocks.final_answer: At \(t = 7\) h (point B); the car then keeps going backward past the start.

blocks.prompt: 2 (c) The displacement-time graph of a moving car is shown in Fig. 7.10. The car changes its direction during the journey, and its motion occurs in three distinct phases. What is the total distance travelled?
blocks.explanation:
Distance is a scalar: every stretch counts as positive, whatever its direction.
Given: the three phases O to A, A to B, B to C.
Plan: add the sizes of the changes in displacement of the three phases.
steps:
Given: O(0, 0), A(3, 60), B(7, 0), C(26/3, -25).
To find: the total distance travelled.
Method: distance = total length of the path travelled, regardless of direction (7.1.1), so we add the sizes of the displacements of the phases.

Size of each stretch
\[O \to A:\ |60 - 0| = 60\]
\[A \to B:\ |0 - 60| = 60\]
\[B \to C:\ |-25 - 0| = 25\]
Why: the absolute value removes the direction and keeps the length of the stretch.

Add
\[60 + 60 + 25 = 145\text{ km}\]
Why: the car really covers all three stretches, so all of them count.

Check
\[145 \ge |-25| \;\checkmark\]
Why: the distance can never be smaller than the size of the total displacement.

blocks.prompt: 2 (d) The displacement-time graph of a moving car is shown in Fig. 7.10. The car changes its direction during the journey, and its motion occurs in three distinct phases. What is the average velocity?
blocks.explanation:
Average velocity uses displacement, not distance, so stretches in opposite directions cancel.
Given: the car starts at x = 0 at t = 0 and ends at x = -25 km at t = 26/3 h.
Plan: total displacement divided by total time.
steps:
Given: start \(O(0, 0)\), end \(C\left(\frac{26}{3}, -25\right)\).
To find: the average velocity.
Method: \(v_{avg} = \frac{\Delta x}{\Delta t}\) (7.1.3).

Total displacement
\[\Delta x = -25 - 0 = -25\text{ km}\]
Why: only the first and the last position matter; the 60 km forward and the 60 km back cancel.

Total time
\[\Delta t = \dfrac{26}{3}\text{ h}\]
Why: from \(t = 0\) to the end of the line, \(t = 7 + \frac{25}{15} = \frac{26}{3}\).

Average velocity
\[v_{avg} = \dfrac{-25}{26/3}\]
\[= -\dfrac{75}{26} \approx -2.88\]
Why: dividing by a fraction means multiplying by its reciprocal: \(-25 \times \frac{3}{26}\).

Check
\[\text{slope of } OC = \dfrac{-25}{26/3} \;\checkmark\]
Why: the average velocity is the slope of the line from the first to the last point. Note the difference: the average speed would be \(145 \div \frac{26}{3} \approx 16.73\) km/h, because speed uses distance.
blocks.final_answer: \(v_{avg} = -\frac{75}{26} \approx -2.88\) km/h (2.88 km/h in the backward direction)
